title: POLICY & PROCEDURE ON STAFF IN-SERVICE TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT
html:
POLICY & PROCEDURE

ON STAFF IN-SERVICE TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT

  • PURPOSE:
    • To provide guide lines on training process to make staff effective to do jobs assigned to them.
    • To have a systematic approach to train and develop Human resources to meet the mission of the organization.
    • To identify training needs precisely and to organize the required training.
    • To have an effective feedback mechanism for assessing the adequacy of training of staff to meet the intended needs.
    • To have evaluation of training effectiveness
    • To plan carry out repeat trainings periodically like nurses training, safety training, etc. to ensure staff are appraised periodically to have proficiency in the respective services
  • SCOPE:

This policy is applicable to all employees (permanent, temporary, probationary, trainee, student or on contract) of the Hospital.

  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Top Management
    • General Manager
    • Matron
    • Human Resources Department
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • AGM: Assistant General Manager
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
    • HRM: Human Resource Management
  • DEFINITION:
    • Permanent Employee:

An employee who has successfully completed his probation period and whose appointment in the permanent vacancy has been confirmed in writing by the AGM – HR & Administration

  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH: NABH Standards for Hospitals
  • POLICY:
    • Training needs identification shall start from the candidate entering the organization in the recruitment phase to enable the candidate to suit the organizational requirements.
    • Other sources of training needs identification shall be:
      • Technology advancement
      • New equipment addition
      • New project introduction
      • When change in job is assigned to the staff
      • Outcome of job evaluation
      • Outcome of department appraisal / Candidate self-appraisal
      • Feedback from audit reports
      • Input from Non-conformance reports and Incident reports
      • Input from continuous improvement program
    • All processes shall identify the staff to be oriented in the respective processes.
    • The training calendar for the entire year shall be established based on the feedback of training needs received from every department.
    • The training methodology shall be established and a trainer, internal or external, shall be identified according to the training needs.
    • Training shall be a continuous process to mould the staff to perform to the best of their ability and to the requirements of the organization.
    • Training shall be the medium of communication to impart knowledge to the staff and to make the process consistent to achieve the intended goals of the process.
    • Where repeat periodic training needs exists like safety practices/ nursing services etc shall be listed down and shall be organized.
    • Training records shall be maintained in HRM or at identified locations and especially they shall be included in the personal records of staff.
    • There shall be mechanism for assessing the effectiveness of trainings done using pre- & post-training documentation evaluation using Quiz / Test.
    • The assessment records shall be maintained by the HR department.
    • There shall be feedback taken from the attendees about the quality of trainings done and towards improvement of training and development program.
  • PROCEDURE:
    • Staff Training:
      • Based on the risk assessment reports of the departments, HR department shall evaluate the potential staff members involved in the operational risks in consultation with Safety coordinators and experts concerned.
      • Based on this evaluation, training needs of the respective staff shall be assessed by HRD and safety expert team concerned.
      • As per the above needs assessed, training shall be scheduled and conducted.
      • The training module shall include making trainees to demonstrate their familiarization on the actions to be taken to report, minimize and eliminate tasks when desired.
      • This training shall be repeated as ongoing program as staff shall have to re-familiarize with them from time to time.
      • The training shall include reporting procedures on common problems, failures and user errors as and when they occur
      • Training also occurs when job responsibilities change / new equipment is introduced.
    • Training Need Identification (TNID) is done by:
      • Direct method and observation – Detail task analysis.
      • Use of questionnaire and Interviews / Records / feedback of supervisions.
      • Attitude Surveys
      • Address to SOP (Standard operating protocol)
    • Task Analysis:
      • Execution of Internal training programs.
      • The data of training needs to be submitted to top management.
      • Top management approves it (If require budget)
      • The personnel department frames and plans and the training.
      • The in charge / Supervision evaluate the effectiveness of training at place.
      • Feedback is taken from the employees.
    • Teaching Methods:
      • Presentations
      • Lectures / Group discussions
      • Supportive documents for demos
    • External Programs:
      • Evaluate the need of training among the employees.
      • Select the employees who should attend it.
      • Get the approval of Top Management.
      • Calculate the cost of training.
      • Keep records / Certificates.
    • Training Records:

Following record is maintained by the HR department:

      • Training calendar
      • Training attendance sheet with name of topic, trainer, date & time, signed by trainees
      • Feedback forms by trainees
      • Question papers solved by trainees to evaluate training effectiveness.
      • Training photographs / videos
      • Training cards of employees
    • Topics for training:
      • Mandatory trainings for all staff:
